label: Red Poll

links.name: Wikipedia: Red Poll (names and herdbook dates)

names.text: 'Red Poll' and its name change to Red Poll in 1888 come from the Wikipedia article, opened with WebFetch. 'Norfolk and Suffolk Red Polled' is from search text (WebSearch, not opened). 'Red Polled' is the older form the search result gives for the name, not checked against a source page; it is included on that basis.

about.text: A hornless English breed formed in East Anglia from Norfolk Red beef cattle and Suffolk Dun dairy cattle. It is now mainly a beef suckler breed, with a few dairy herds in England and Texas. Its milk was once valued, but historical yield figures are anecdotal.

sources.text: Wikipedia, opened with WebFetch: origin from Norfolk Red and Suffolk Dun, current use as beef suckler cows with a few dairy herds in England and Texas. The 'milk was once valued' point is from the search text and the Livestock Conservancy page (WebSearch text, not opened); the yield anecdotes are not stated as fact here.

links.name: History of the Red Poll Cattle Breed (redpoll.org)

sources.text: Wikipedia, opened with WebFetch: developed in England in the late 19th century, cross of Norfolk Red and Suffolk Dun, first herd book 1874, society formed 1888. The 1846 date (recognition) comes from WebSearch text (not opened), and the 1874 herdbook is the earlier of the two sources' dates. Range is 1846 to 1874 for the formation of the breed; the 1874 herdbook date is the firm one.
Wikipedia, opened with WebFetch: described as dual-purpose, with its main role beef (suckler cows); a few dairy herds in England and Texas.

facts.v: Florabel (10862) gave 108,310.5 lb of milk over eleven years in the United States, which was an all-breed record in 1933.

sources.text: Seen in WebSearch text, not opened: Livestock Conservancy report of Florabel's eleven-year total and the 1933 all-breed record. Figure is in pounds as given.

facts.v: Listed by the Livestock Conservancy among its Conservation Priority Breeds.

sources.text: Wikipedia, opened with WebFetch: lists the breed under 'Conservation Priority Breeds of the Livestock Conservancy'.

gaps: No FAO DAD-IS record, population figure or risk status found (DAD-IS was not searched directly). No yield figures from a usable source: the Wikipedia article gives none, and the milk record above is a single cow. No composition figures found. The 1846 date conflicts with the 1863 and 1873-74 dates in the search results, so the origin range is wide.
